change.title: pr-10
change.description: FEATURE: Can edit category/host relationships for embedding
change.author: Robin Ward

findings.title: Migration crashes on any site that never set embed_category
findings.body: `execute(...)[0]['id']` assumes the join returned a row. `embed_category` defaults to `''` (config/site_settings.yml at base), so a site that never changed it has no `site_settings` row, and the join also finds nothing when the stored name matches no category. In both cases `[0]` on the empty PG::Result raises (IndexError, or NoMethodError on nil), so `rake db:migrate` fails on most installs. The fallback on line 15 has the same problem when `uncategorized_category_id` has no row. Check `cmd_tuples > 0` or `ntuples` before indexing, as line 19 already does.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are stored raw and many will never match a referer
findings.body: Values are copied from the old setting unchanged. The old `allows_embeddable_host?` took entries like `http://eviltrout.com` and `https://example.com/1234`; base site_setting_spec tested both. It also took entries with trailing `\r` or spaces. The new `record_for_host` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17) compares against the bare `uri.host`, so these rows never match. After upgrading, embedding stops working (InvalidAccess) for those sites, and nothing tells the admin why. The model's `before_validation` normalisation is skipped because this is raw SQL. Strip the scheme, path and whitespace, and skip blank entries, before inserting. The value is also interpolated into SQL unquoted: an entry containing `'` aborts the migration. Use `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote`.

findings.title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
findings.body: `self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when `host` is nil. That happens when `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` is missing (embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:23), so the admin gets a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard it, e.g. `self.host = host.to_s.sub(...).sub(...)` or `return if host.blank?`.

findings.title: Host lookup is case-sensitive on the referer side and ignores ports
findings.body: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the column but not the argument. As far as I can tell, `URI(...).host` keeps the case it is given, so a referer like `http://EvilTrout.com/x` is rejected. Use `host.downcase`. Separately, the validation on line 2 accepts `example.com:8080`, but `uri.host` never includes the port. A host saved with a port can therefore never match, and the admin is told nothing. Either reject ports in validation or compare against host plus port.

findings.title: Imported topics lose their category when the URL host has no EmbeddableHost row
findings.body: Before, every embed import went to `SiteSetting.embed_category`. Now the category comes only from the EmbeddableHost row that matches the URL's host. Some imports have no such row, for example feed-polling imports whose article host differs from the embedding host. Those now go to `nil` (uncategorized), and there is no site-wide fallback. Please confirm this is intended for feed-polling users.

findings.title: Unknown id gives a 500 instead of a 404
findings.body: `where(id: ...).first` returns nil for an unknown id, so `host.destroy` here and `save_host(nil)` in `update` (line 10) raise NoMethodError. Use `find` (which gives a 404) or `raise Discourse::NotFound`.

findings.title: Failed delete is silent
findings.body: `destroyRecord()` has no `.catch(popupAjaxError)`, unlike `save` on line 40. If the request fails, the row stays and the admin sees no error.

findings.title: saveChanges action and the PUT endpoint are unused
findings.body: No template triggers `saveChanges`. `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` (and the `put customize/embedding` route) only re-renders the object without changing anything. Remove them, or wire them up if they are meant for later.

findings.title: `hydrated || []` is dead code, and missing ids leave undefined entries
findings.body: `Array#map` always returns an array, so the `|| []` never applies. `_lookupSubType` (line 157) returns undefined when an id is not in the root collection, and those undefined entries end up in the array. A null `*_ids` value throws on `.map`. Consider `(obj[k] || []).map(...).filter(Boolean)`.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents are swapped
findings.body: category_fabricator.rb now defines `:embeddable_host`, and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines all the category fabricators. It works, but anyone looking for a fabricator will open the wrong file. Swap the contents back.

findings.title: "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer tests that
findings.body: `expandable_first_post?` no longer looks at embeddable hosts (app/models/topic.rb:869). This example passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and `has_topic_embed?` is false for a built topic. The `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` in the nested `before` on line 1409 is likewise irrelevant. Rename the example or remove it.

findings.title: Test asks for fruit 2 but asserts fruit 1's colors
findings.body: The pretender's `/fruits/:id` always returns `fruits[0]` (create-pretender.js.es6:227), so `find('fruit', 2)` gets apple, with `color_ids: [1,2]`. The assertions pass only because of that. Use `find('fruit', 1)`, or make the pretender honour `:id`.

contracts.action: Migration moves embeddable_hosts/embed_category site settings into a table, then DELETEs both settings
contracts.equivalent_path: Old SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? read the setting directly
contracts.before_after: Before: entries with a scheme or path were accepted. After: they are copied raw and fail record_for_host's exact host compare.
contracts.visible_effect: Embedding breaks (InvalidAccess) for sites whose hosts had http:// or a path; the old setting is gone, so the admin cannot see the original value.
contracts.failure_mode: If embed_category has no row, line 11 raises and the whole migration aborts (Postgres DDL runs in a transaction, so the DELETE does not run on its own). The DELETE targets only the two named settings, and those rows were read in the same transaction.

contracts.action: Admin deletes an embeddable host from the Embedding page
contracts.before_after: New screen; the delete targets the row id the admin clicked.
contracts.visible_effect: On success the row is removed via deleteHost → removeObject.
contracts.failure_mode: A rejected destroyRecord is not caught, so the error is silent and the row stays. On the server, an unknown id gives a 500.

contracts.action: Embedding admin page loads hosts via store.find('embedding') with embeddable_host_ids hydration
contracts.before_after: New *_ids branch maps each id through _lookupSubType against root.embeddable_hosts.
contracts.visible_effect: Hosts are listed in the table sorted by host.
contracts.failure_mode: Missing ids become undefined entries; a fetch error leaves the route in its error state.

summary:
This PR moves the embeddable-host allowlist from a site setting into its own table, with an admin screen to manage it. Blocker: the migration indexes `[0]` on an empty result when the `embed_category` setting was never set, which is the default, so `db:migrate` fails on most sites. Also to fix in this PR:
- The migration copies legacy entries such as `http://host` or `host/path` unchanged, so they never match a referer and embedding silently breaks for those sites.
- The SQL insert interpolates the host value without quoting.
- `before_validation` crashes on a nil host.
- The host lookup lowercases the stored host but not the referer's, and hosts saved with a port can never match.
The remaining findings are smaller: a delete error that is never shown, dead code, misnamed fabricator files, and tests that pass for the wrong reason.
